speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for your patience. To begin our evaluation, can you describe exactly how the swelling started and if you have noticed any skin color changes, such as redness or warmth over the affected area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That sounds like a significant traumatic injury. Given the mechanism of injury, could you tell me if you felt or heard a "pop" at the moment of impact, and are you currently able to fully flex and extend your finger?

REQUEST IMAGES: Hand_X-Ray_right_ring_finger

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Terminal Extensor Avulsion)

Based on your inability to actively flex the distal interphalangeal joint while the finger extends in a resting position, this is classic for a mallet finger injury resulting from the forceful pull you described. I have requested a hand X-ray to confirm if there is an associated fracture of the distal phalanx, which would change the treatment protocol.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
